macros.name: boxput
macros.doc: You might use \boxput to put a “water mark” in the background of a box, or to put a label next to a box, when you don’t want this label to take up any space.

macros.name: boxput*
macros.doc: You might use \boxput to put a “water mark” in the background of a box, or to put a label next to a box, when you don’t want this label to take up any space.

macros.name: EveryVerbatim
macros.doc: \EveryVerbatim Whatever else you want to say before formatting the verbatim text. By default, it does nothing.

macros.name: EveryVerbatimLine
macros.doc: \EveryVerbatimLine This is inserted at the beginning of each line of verbatim environments or verbatim files. By default it does nothing.

macros.name: GenericCaption
macros.doc: fancybox.sty defines a generic caption, \GenericCaption, that doesn’t affect the numbering of floats, doesn’t make an entry in a list of floats, and doesn’t add anything to the argument you give.

macros.name: Landscape
macros.doc: You can use \LandScape, \Landscape and \Landscape*, rather then the LandScape, Landscape and Landscape* environments, if you want the rest of the document to be in landscape mode.

macros.name: Landscape*
macros.doc: You can use \LandScape, \Landscape and \Landscape*, rather then the LandScape, Landscape and Landscape* environments, if you want the rest of the document to be in landscape mode.

macros.name: LandScape
macros.doc: You can use \LandScape, \Landscape and \Landscape*, rather then the LandScape, Landscape and Landscape* environments, if you want the rest of the document to be in landscape mode.

macros.name: Ovalbox
macros.doc: \Ovalbox This is like \ovalbox, except that the width of the lines is set by the \thicklines declaration.

macros.name: shadowsize
macros.doc: The width of the shadow is \shadowsize (default: 4pt).

macros.name: thisfancyput
macros.doc: \thisfancyput affects only the current page, and is a global declaration (analogous to \thispagestyle).

macros.name: thisfancyput*
macros.doc: \thisfancyput affects only the current page, and is a global declaration (analogous to \thispagestyle).

macros.name: UseVerb
macros.doc: Like \UseVerbatim, but without any particular formatting.

macros.name: VerbatimFont
macros.doc: The font to use for verbatim text.

macros.name: VerbatimFootnotes
macros.doc: For footnotes, put the command \VerbatimFootnotes in the preamble, and then you can use verbatim commands or environments in the argument of \footnote.

macros.name: VerbatimFuzz
macros.doc: This is the amount by which lines can be too long in a Verbatim or LVerbatim environment before you get overfull \hbox warnings.

envs.name: Beqnarray
envs.doc: fancybox.sty contains a Beqnarray environment, which is like the eqnarray environment but it is not vertical mode material.

envs.name: Beqnarray*
envs.doc: fancybox.sty contains a Beqnarray environment, which is like the eqnarray environment but it is not vertical mode material.

envs.name: BVerbatim
envs.doc: Produces a box with the same width as the longest verbatim line.

envs.name: BVerbatim
envs.doc: Produces a box with the same width as the longest verbatim line.

envs.name: landfloat
envs.doc: If the whole document is in landscape mode, then landfloat gives you a portrait-mode float—good for a table that is too tall to fit in landscape mode.

envs.name: LVerbatim
envs.doc: Like Verbatim, but list rather than trivlist is used to display the listing, and so it is indented from the left margin.

envs.name: SaveVerbatim
envs.doc: Saves the verbatim text as cmd. cmd is defined globally, without checking whether cmd is already defined.

envs.name: Sbox
envs.doc: fancybox.sty contains an Sbox environment that makes it easy to define your own LR-box environments.

envs.name: Verbatim
envs.doc: Works pretty much like LaTeX’s verbatim.

envs.name: VerbatimOut
envs.doc: Writes the verbatim text to file.
